config.title: Recursive TreeView

intro.title: Recursive TreeView
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Recursive TreeView component in Angular, which visually displays hierarchical data like a file system or organizational chart. You will learn how to use recursion, a programming technique where a component calls itself to handle nested structures. The main technologies involved are Angular components, TypeScript interfaces for defining tree node data, and Angular's template syntax for conditional rendering. By the end, you will understand how to create a dynamic, self-repeating UI component that can handle any depth of nested data.
intro.usecase: Recursive TreeView patterns are essential for displaying hierarchical data in enterprise applications. You'll find them in file explorers like VS Code's sidebar, where folders contain subfolders and files in nested structures. They're also used in organizational charts, nested comment threads on platforms like Reddit, and category navigation menus in e-commerce sites where categories have subcategories. As an Angular developer, you'll implement these to create scalable navigation systems and data management interfaces that users can expand and collapse intuitively.

objectives: Construct a recursive Angular component that renders nested tree data
Initialize and bind component state to represent hierarchical tree nodes
Implement click handlers to control the expansion and collapse of tree branches
Configure component inputs to accept dynamic tree data structures
Apply conditional rendering to display nested child nodes recursively
Manipulate component state to track which tree nodes are currently expanded
Integrate the recursive TreeView component into a parent application view

steps.title: Import Component and CommonModule from @angular/core and @angular/common
steps.instruction: Import the Component decorator from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common' to prepare for creating an Angular component.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import specific symbols from Angular packages.
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports are added at the top of the file, enabling component creation and Angular directives.
successCriteria: Component is imported from '@angular/core' and CommonModule is imported from '@angular/common'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both Component and CommonModule from their respective packages.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Check that you're importing Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.

steps.title: Define TreeNode interface for tree data structure
steps.instruction: Below the imports, define a TypeScript interface named TreeNode with the following properties: label (string), children (TreeNode[]), and expanded (boolean, optional).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions with type annotations. Make expanded optional by adding a '?' after the property name.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component, CommonModule } from '@angular/core';

// Define TreeNode interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a TreeNode interface that defines the structure for tree nodes with typed properties.
successCriteria: TreeNode interface is defined with label (string), children (TreeNode[]), and optional expanded (boolean) properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Check that you have all three properties with correct types: label (string), children (TreeNode[]), and optional expanded (boolean).
steps.feedbackWrong: The TreeNode interface definition is missing or incorrect. Make sure to define an interface with label, children, and optional expanded properties.

steps.title: Create TreeViewComponent class with Component decorator
steps.instruction: Create a class named TreeViewComponent and decorate it with @Component, setting selector to 'app-tree-view' and standalone to true.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from '@angular/core' that you imported earlier. The class should be exported.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a TreeViewComponent class ready to be used as a standalone Angular component.
successCriteria: TreeViewComponent class is created, decorated with @Component, has selector 'app-tree-view', and standalone: true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the class is named TreeViewComponent, uses @Component with selector 'app-tree-view' and standalone: true.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class is missing or incomplete. Check that you've created TreeViewComponent with the @Component decorator.

steps.title: Add imports array with CommonModule to component decorator
steps.instruction: Inside the @Component decorator of your TreeViewComponent, add an imports property with an array containing CommonModule.
steps.hint: The imports array configures which Angular modules this component can use. Add it as a property in the decorator object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component decorator now includes an imports array with CommonModule, enabling Angular directives in the template.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator has an imports property set to [CommonModule].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added an imports property inside the @Component decorator object, with its value set to an array containing CommonModule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component decorator still needs an imports array with CommonModule. Check that you've added the property correctly inside the decorator object.

steps.title: Define input property for tree nodes with TreeNode type
steps.instruction: Add an input property named 'nodes' to the TreeViewComponent class to accept tree data from a parent component. Use the TreeNode interface type and initialize it with an empty array.
steps.hint: Use Angular's @Input decorator to define the property. Remember to import Input if needed (it's already imported from '@angular/core').
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a properly typed input property ready to receive tree data.
successCriteria: The TreeViewComponent has an @Input() property named 'nodes' of type TreeNode[] initialized as an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've used @Input(), named the property 'nodes', typed it as TreeNode[], and initialized it with an empty array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input property isn't correctly defined. Check that you've used @Input(), named it 'nodes', given it the TreeNode[] type, and initialized it with [].

steps.title: Create toggle method to expand/collapse tree nodes
steps.instruction: Inside the TreeViewComponent class, define a method named toggle that takes a TreeNode parameter and toggles an expanded property on that node.
steps.hint: Add a method to the class that modifies the node's state. You'll need to add the expanded property to the TreeNode interface first.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a toggle method that can expand/collapse tree nodes by modifying their expanded state.
successCriteria: TreeViewComponent contains a toggle method that accepts a TreeNode parameter and toggles an expanded property on that node.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but check if it properly toggles an expanded property on the TreeNode. The method should modify the node's state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggle method is missing or incorrect. Make sure you define a method named toggle that takes a TreeNode parameter and toggles its expanded property.

steps.title: Add template structure with ng-container for recursive rendering
steps.instruction: Inside the TreeViewComponent class decorator, add a template property with an ng-container that uses *ngFor to iterate through nodes.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator's template property with Angular's structural directives.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a template structure ready for recursive rendering.
successCriteria: Component has a template property with ng-container and *ngFor directive.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the template property with ng-container and *ngFor.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure is missing or incorrect. Check the syntax for ng-container and *ngFor.

steps.title: Add node display with label and expand/collapse indicator
steps.instruction: Inside the ng-container in your template, add a span element to display the node's label and a button with a plus/minus icon to indicate expand/collapse state.
steps.hint: Use Angular's template syntax to output the node label and create a button that calls the toggle method when clicked.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now displays each node's label and includes an interactive button to expand/collapse child nodes.
successCriteria: The ng-container contains a span showing {{ node.label }} and a button with (click)="toggle(node)" that displays '+' or '-' based on expansion state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added both the span for the label and the button with click handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet show node labels or expand/collapse controls. Add a span for the label and a button that calls the toggle method.

steps.title: Wire toggle method to expand/collapse button click
steps.instruction: Add a (click) event binding to the expand/collapse button in your template that calls the toggle method with the current node as an argument.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax: (click)="toggle(node)" on the button element.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: wiring a click event to a method
<button (click)="handleClick(item)">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The expand/collapse button will have a click event handler that calls the toggle method with the current node.
successCriteria: The template contains a button with (click)="toggle(node)" event binding.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the button has (click)="toggle(node)" with the node parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button doesn't have the correct click event binding. It should call toggle(node).

steps.title: Add recursive TreeViewComponent for child nodes
steps.instruction: Inside the ng-container, after the node display, add an <app-tree-view> component with *ngIf to conditionally render child nodes when the node is expanded, passing the node's children via the [nodes] input binding.
steps.hint: Use *ngIf="node.expanded" on a wrapper element (like a div) that contains the recursive <app-tree-view> component. Bind [nodes]="node.children" to pass the child nodes.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will include a recursive <app-tree-view> component that renders child nodes when the parent node is expanded, completing the recursive tree view implementation.
successCriteria: The template contains an <app-tree-view> component inside a conditional *ngIf wrapper that checks node.expanded, with [nodes] binding to node.children.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the <app-tree-view> component with *ngIf="node.expanded" and bound [nodes]="node.children".
steps.feedbackWrong: The recursive component isn't properly implemented. Check that you've added <app-tree-view> with the correct conditional rendering and input binding.
